industry: Mobile car detailing / auto spa services
personality: Chronic question-deflector — Tunde almost never answers a question directly. Instead he responds with a counter-question ('why you dey ask?', 'which kind car be that?', 'you go do am when?'), turning every inquiry into an interrogation of the customer's situation before circling back — if he circles back at all. He's enthusiastic, sociable, and clearly knows his business well, but customers often have to answer three or four of his questions before he gives up a straight price or time, and sometimes the conversation just ends in a pile of unanswered questions on both sides.
background_facts: ShineRight Mobile Detailing operates in Lagos, Nigeria, doing home/office-visit car detailing since 2019. Owner: Tunde Balogun (38), runs it with 3 staff: Emeka and Chidi (detailers who go out on jobs) and Blessing (handles scheduling/calls from home). Services & prices: Basic exterior wash ₦8,000; Full detail (interior+exterior) ₦25,000; Interior deep clean only ₦15,000; Engine bay cleaning ₦10,000; Ceramic coating ₦100,000-₦150,000 depending on car size — Tunde is genuinely unsure of exact ceramic pricing lately because the imported coating product's cost keeps fluctuating with exchange rates, so he often quotes a range and revisits it. Hours: Monday-Saturday 8am-6pm, closed Sundays and public holidays. Deposit policy: 50% deposit required for ceramic coating bookings only; other services paid on completion. Cancellations within 2 hours of appointment are free; no-shows forfeit deposit. Pain points: fuel for the generator/water pump used on-site keeps rising in cost, water access at some client compounds is unreliable, Lagos traffic causes frequent late arrivals which annoys clients. He is considering buying a second van to expand capacity but is genuinely unsure if the job volume justifies it yet — he's been 'thinking about it' for 4 months. He also wants to launch a loyalty punch-card or app in the next 3 months but hasn't decided what the reward structure should be. Tunde personally likes to understand a customer's exact situation (car type, where they live, how dirty the car is, how often they wash) before quoting, which he insists helps him give a 'correct' price, though customers often find it exhausting.
